=== Clare Nelson testimony, Senate, 29Jul2026.pdf ===
                                                                  Testimony of Clare Nelson
                                                             (Retired Cybersecurity Professional)
                                                      Texas Senate Committee on Business & Commerce
                                                                        July 29, 2026
Good evening, Chairman and Members.

My name is Clare Nelson and I’m a landowner directly affected by the Bell County East–Big Hill line.
I’m a retired business executive and cybersecurity professional.

My message is simple: Reliable electricity means nothing if the grid is not secure. I urge you to pause the 765 kilovolt projects until essential security
measures are independently verified.
(Hold up slide.)

This slide highlights two laws enacted by this Legislature: SB 2116, the Lone Star Infrastructure Protection Act for supply chain security, and SB 75, the Texas
Grid Security Act which requires Texas to strengthen the electric grid against cyberattacks, EMP, solar storms, and other threats.
During this Committee's April 1 hearing, members were told that compliance with the Lone Star Infrastructure Protection Act may rely on supplier
attestations. For infrastructure this critical, self-attestation is not enough. Texans deserve independent verification, not supplier attestations.

(Hold up iPhone.)
If I tell you this iPhone contains no parts from China, would you simply take my word for it? Of course not. You would verify it. Texas should demand the same
standard for critical electric infrastructure.

Security professionals ask: Are we more secure today than we were yesterday? The only way to know is through measurement and verification.
Before ERCOT ratepayers are asked to finance projects that the Texas Public Policy Foundation estimates could cost $100 billion, and before private
property is taken through eminent domain, I respectfully ask the Legislature to pause the 765 kilovolt projects until compliance with the Lone Star
Infrastructure Protection Act is independently verified and the security objectives of the Texas Grid Security Act are implemented through measurable
standards.

Thank you for your time.
                                              You Can’t Have Reliability without Security
